---
argmap-version: 0.3
title: "Can We Govern Superintelligence? (Tang vs Shapira)"
author: "debate extraction round 1 (LLM-extracted from the episode transcript, single elicitor)"
date: 2026-07-19
source: "https://lironshapira.substack.com/p/can-we-govern-superintelligence-taiwans"
speakers:
  l: "Liron Shapira (host, Doom Debates; argues the Yudkowskian doom case)"
  a: "Audrey Tang (Taiwan Cyber Ambassador-at-large; plurality / foomer-not-doomer case)"
  al: "joint: explicitly shared or conceded by both speakers"
focus: [everyone-dies]
related-maps: "iabied-comprehensive-en.argmap: shared statement ids reused where the proposition coincides (@everyone-dies, @whether-vs-when, @opaque); near-misses deliberately NOT co-named (@prepare-pause is the weaker debate analogue of the book map's @shutdown)"
description: >
  The Doom Debates episode "Taiwan's Cyber Ambassador-At-Large Says Humans &
  AI Can FOOM Together" (Liron Shapira vs Audrey Tang, published 2026-01-20,
  ~1h52m), extracted as the pilot of the multi-voice conventions
  (ideas/plans/archive/content-debate-tang.md). ONE map, TWO voices: statements
  are speaker-neutral propositions and carry NO pins (their posteriors come
  entirely from the mapped factors); every evidence is attributed to its
  asserter by id prefix ($l- / $a- / $al-), repeated as an "L: / A: / AL:"
  label prefix so attribution stays visible on the graph and outline surfaces,
  which show labels, not ids. Each evidence also carries a strength from that
  speaker's verbatim spoken register via the pre-registered R-SPOKEN table
  (AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-07-19 debate entry) and, since the 2026-09-12 pass, a
  `# kind:` key from the K-SPOKEN reading of the D161 rubric (AUTHORING_NOTES
  2026-09-12), which says how firmly the step is held rather than how likely
  it is. All rubric-derived strengths keep the `?` marker; bare numbers are
  reserved for numbers a speaker stated as numbers. A credence a speaker
  stated as a number sits in the statement's `# check:` slot (D39, D156),
  which the format gives ONE of per statement: where both speakers price the
  same proposition the second number stays in the trailing comment, and that
  gap is the map's standing argument for a two-author extension
  (AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-12 lists the three instances). Tang's REFUSAL of a
  point P(doom) ("the interval is the message") is rendered as blankness, not
  as 0.5. Verbatim spoken words sit on `>` quote lines with their transcript
  timestamp as the locator (D59), so the gloss reads as a claim and the words
  that carry it stay walkable back to the source. Five declared groups (D58)
  box the single-voice batteries, one speaker per box, so a reader can fold a
  whole case and see whose it was. Where the speakers concur
  NON-diametrically, the two-voice overlap discipline applies (AUTHORING_NOTES
  2026-07-19 addendum): full concurrence merges to one $al- line
  (author-the-weaker); subset claims split into a shared $al- part plus a
  single-voice residual re-elicited conditional on it; instance-of claims are
  rerouted to support the shared ground, so no agreed content is
  double-counted by the independent-factor accounting.
  Reading the solve: the whole-map solved value is a POOLED agent believing
  both speakers' factors at once, so it is neither speaker's credence and no
  node here should be read as "the debate's answer"; per-speaker projections
  (filter by prefix) are the disagreement readout and remain an open tracker
  item (ideas/tracker/solver.md [P3]).
---

# ============================================================
# SPINE: the debate is meta-shaped. The doom proposition (@everyone-dies)
# is barely argued directly; the fight is over (1) whether a credence on it
# is even assignable (@priceable -> @doom-material), (2) the shared "can"
# axis both speakers grant (@ceiling-high, @rsi-plausible, @deadly-capable,
# @can-vs-will), (3) the crux: @aligned-in-time — Tang's plural/interpretable
# takeoff vs Shapira's no-iterations mainline — feeding @everyone-dies via
# the jointly-granted conditional $al-if-unaligned, and (4) the policy fork
# @prepare-pause vs @measure-then-sunset.
# Nesting: each cluster folds under its local conclusion statement; shared
# ground referenced across clusters stays a top-level cluster head (@opaque,
# @post-attention, the section-4 "can" axis, @dividends-needed, @oom-slices)
# so it cannot fold away with a cluster that borrows it. Since the
# 2026-08-03 spine-surfacing pass, the evidences that LINK cluster heads to
# each other are top-level too ($l-material, $a-material-uc, $al-foom,
# $al-can, $l-pause, $a-montreal, alongside the original $al-if-unaligned),
# so the collapsed view shows the debate's shape instead of a wall of
# disconnected heads (spine test, W21); what folds under a head is its own
# intra-cluster support and objection traffic. Same-day tier pass: the
# Harari sub-debate (@slow-steers-fast and its lines) is consumed nowhere
# outside section 6, so it folds under @gardener-model and that block
# collapses to one card. The remaining heads are irreducible: the can-axis
# and @foom-soon are shared into @aligned-in-time's internal battle, and
# the rest are genuinely separate blocks (I2 lists nine). `focus:` declares
# the map's terminus (@everyone-dies), D57.
# Excluded as argumentatively thin (scope discipline, see FINDINGS round 5):
# the chips-geopolitics chapter, biography segments, most positive-program
# detail (Green Earth, 6-pack pack-by-pack, Softmax) beyond what carries
# inferential load. Transcript turn-label glitch 01:10:44-01:11:21 noted in
# FINDINGS; attribution there recovered from content.
# 2026-09-12 format pass: `# check:` on the three statements a speaker priced
# as a number, `# kind:` on all 45 strengthed lines (K-SPOKEN rubric, fixed
# before assignment, single pass, AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-12), and `>` quote
# lines carrying the verbatim spoken words each line rests on. Five declared
# groups (D58), one per single-voice battery, replace the `# --` banner
# comments no tool could see: three in the credence dispute (::nan-case,
# ::ballpark-case, ::glass-condition) and two at the crux (::tang-routes,
# ::shapira-record). Each is nested rather than document-level, so the W12
# whole-block rule does not bite, and each folds to a summary card.
# The 15 premise-less direct-assertion floors are unchanged and draw the I4
# reading note by design. Only @below-optimal-fear carries two floors, and
# they are the overlap discipline's shared span plus Shapira's residual,
# not one assertion twice, so they stay separate (and two is below W27's
# three-floor threshold).
# ============================================================

# ---- 1. The doom proposition and the credence dispute ----

@everyone-dies [AI kills everyone]: extinction-level catastrophe from artificial superintelligence, the shared subject of the debate (id shared with iabied-comprehensive)  # check: 0.1..0.9 is Shapira's stated ballpark. Tang states no point: her likelihood is flat over the whole board and she calls its mean cosmetic, and she rejects the ten percent he later attributes to her. Two speakers, one check slot: the two-author gap, instance 1
  > I feel like ten to ninety percent is the ballpark. So what is your ballpark? [^t001942]
  > It is from zero percent to one hundred percent. We’re flying blind. We don’t know. So the mean, I guess, is fifty percent, but it’s cosmetic. The interval is the message. [^t001734]
  > I model you as effectively having a P(Doom) that’s, let’s say, ten percent, in the ballpark of ten percent. [^t014650]
  > I don’t think so. No, I really don’t think so. [^t014721]

@opaque [Frontier transformer models are opaque]: internals measurable but not reliably interpretable: "wooden Trojan horses that we literally don't know what's inside" (id shared with iabied-comprehensive; here asserted from Tang's own interpretability case; shared ground for $a-nan and $a-material-uc, so it stays a top-level head) [^t002043]
  > we can measure some of the internals, but we cannot reliably interpret them [^t001734]
  > so not the current wooden Trojan horses that we literally don’t know what’s inside, whether it’s going to do a sharp left turn or maybe a sharp right turn, you don’t know [^t002043]
  $a-blur [A: attention is a blur of what causes what] 0.9? @opaque: the quadratic self-attention transformer "literally is a blur of what causes what". We don't know where the plane hides its intentions, or whether it does [^t005008]  # kind: mechanism
    > I think a lot of the current muddiness is because of the quadratic self-attention transformer architecture, which literally is a blur of what causes what. [^t005008]
    > And so because of this, we don’t even know where the plane is actually hiding its intentions or whether it’s hiding its intentions. [^t005008]

@priceable [A meaningful credence on AI doom is assignable today]: can one responsibly state a number or range for P(doom) under current interpretability?  # audrey: NaN [^t001734]; liron: clearly yes [^t001837]
  > My P(Doom) is NaN, or Not A Number, and here’s why. [^t001734]
  # Three single-voice batteries, one declared box each (D58): her case
  # against assignability, his case for a ballpark anyway, and the
  # condition under which she would price it. The slicing support and
  # $a-glass are left as independent factors deliberately: disjoint
  # mechanisms (his slicing works TODAY; hers is conditional on
  # @interp-deployed), so the overlap discipline does not collapse them.
  # @oom-slices is homed at TOP LEVEL below (burial test: $l-material in
  # the next cluster consumes it too).
  ::nan-case [A: why she will not give a number]: Tang's battery against assignability: the risk formula needs a visibility term the architecture does not supply, and the claim is unsettleable in our horizon.
    > we’re trying to compute a value where the inspection term is missing, like dividing by zero or something [^t001734]
    @risk-needs-vis [Risk assessment requires visibility]: her operating model: risk = capability / visibility; with the inspection term missing the division is undefined [^t001734]
      > If you think of risk as capability divided by visibility, the story looks simple, right? The numerator is climbing fast. Everyone sees it climb. [^t001734]
      $a-nuclear [A: the nuclear contrast case] 0.8? @risk-needs-vis: where visibility exists she prices risk: "somebody has to launch that nuclear missile", so her nuclear-doom credence is "much more standard shaped" (mean ~0.5 by 2100, narrower variance) [^t002115] [^t002150]  # kind: analogy
        > I think for nuclear, it’s much more interpretable because somebody has to launch that nuclear missile. And so my P(Doom) for nuclear is much more standard shaped. So yeah, my nuclear variance is quite narrower. [^t002115]
        > Yeah, so I think I’ll put it roughly around fifty percent, and— [^t002150]
    $a-nan [A: the NaN argument] 0.9? ~@priceable | @opaque AND @risk-needs-vis: with interpretability missing the likelihood function is flat over 0-100%; "the mean, I guess, is fifty percent, but it's cosmetic. The interval is the message. The calculation simply does not converge unless you have real interpretability" [^t001734]  # kind: deductive
      > But if the likelihood function is broken, it literally looks like a flat line, right? It covers the entire board. [^t001734]
      > The calculation simply does not converge unless you have real interpretability. [^t001734]
    @unverifiable-epoch [The doom claim can't be settled in our horizon]: the coin flipped into outer space: "by the time it lands, I'm probably not here anymore" [^t001905]
      > Okay, but it’s flipping into outer space. By the time it lands, I’m probably not here anymore. [^t001905]
    $a-coin [A: no standing to call the outlier wrong] 0.7? ~@priceable | @unverifiable-epoch AND $l-slices: undercut of the slicing move. Without a settleable event, "what position do I have to say that they're probably wrong?", even against the one-in-a-million claimant [^t001905]  # kind: testimony
      > So what position do I have to say that they’re probably wrong? [^t001905]
  ::ballpark-case [L: why a ballpark is assignable anyway]: Shapira's battery for a range: geometric slicing plus a background-risk floor make ten to ninety percent a statement rather than noise.
    > I mean, there’s clearly a ballpark. I feel like ten to ninety percent is the ballpark. [^t001942]
    @asteroid-floor [Background risks set a meaningful floor]: "once you get to one in a hundred million, you're just talking about yearly asteroid impacts", so sub-one-in-a-million P(doom) claims are clearly wrong [^t001942]
      > I mean, once you get to one in a hundred million, you’re just talking about yearly asteroid impacts, right? [^t001942]
    $l-slices [L: odds-ratio slicing licenses a ballpark] 0.85? @priceable | @oom-slices AND @asteroid-floor: even under deep uncertainty, geometric slicing plus reference floors make "ten to ninety percent is the ballpark" a defensible statement, not noise [^t001837] [^t001942]  # kind: deductive
      > because geometrically speaking, ten to ninety percent, that’s one slice. Ninety to ninety-nine percent, that’s another slice. Ninety-nine to ninety-nine point nine, that’s another slice. [^t001942]
  ::glass-condition [A: the number she would give]: her refusal is conditional, and this box names the condition.
    > and then I’ll give you a real number [^t002043]
    @interp-deployed [Inspectable architecture is a deployment condition]: frontier systems have "bounded, inspectable state" (a glass horse, not a wooden one) as a condition of deployment [^t002043]
      > And also, I think we need architecture with bounded, with inspectable state [^t002043]
    $a-glass [A: the refusal is conditional, not absolute] 0.85? @priceable | @interp-deployed: "we need a glass horse system that you can actually see into as a condition of deployment, and then I'll give you a real number" [^t002043]  # kind: testimony
      > But we need a glass horse system that you can actually see into as a condition of deployment, and then I’ll give you a real number. [^t002043]

@oom-slices [Order-of-magnitude slices make wide ranges meaningful]: 10-90% is one geometric slice (1:1 odds), 90-99% the next (10:1). Jan Leike's much-mocked "ten to ninety percent" was "actually a much smarter statement than it sounds like". Shared ground for $l-slices above and $l-material below, so it stays a top-level head [^t001942]
  > And when you think about it as an odds ratio, it’s like one to one versus ten to one versus a hundred to one. [^t001942]
  > People made fun of him for being meaningless. I’m like, “No, that’s not meaningless,” [^t001942]

@doom-material [AI doom risk is material, well above 1%]:  # liron: obviously [^t002243]; audrey declines even this: "we literally don't know" [^t002247]
$l-material [L: materiality follows a fortiori] 0.9? @doom-material | @priceable AND @oom-slices: if 10-90% is the ballpark, "obviously, AI doom is more than one percent" [^t002243]  # kind: deductive
  > But you’re not willing to say, “Okay, obviously, AI doom is more than one percent.” You’re not willing to say that? [^t002243]
$a-material-uc [A: non-convergence blocks the materiality call too] 0.9? ~@doom-material | @opaque AND $l-material: undercut: asked to affirm even >1%, "That's right... Because we don't know. We literally don't know" [^t002247]  # kind: testimony
  > Because we don’t know. We literally don’t know. [^t002247]

# ---- 2. The shared priority (the CAIS statement) ----

@xrisk-priority [AI extinction risk is a global priority]: the CAIS statement verbatim: mitigating extinction risk from AI belongs alongside pandemics and nuclear war [^t002253]
  > The statement says, “Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks, such as pandemics and nuclear war.” [^t002253]
  $al-statement [AL: both endorse the statement] 0.85? @xrisk-priority: Tang signed as the inaugural signatory and stands by it heading into 2026 ("mitigating starts with measuring"); Shapira cites it approvingly "all the time" [^t002321] [^t002512]  # kind: testimony
    > I want the entire world to know that we currently know almost nothing about the actual shape of AI risks, and which is why I signed [^t002321]
    > And mitigating starts with measuring, yes. [^t002512]

@dividends-needed [Mitigation must pay chronic dividends to persist]: risk work whose only visible success is "nothing happens" decays politically (shared ground; also premised by $a-montreal in section 7) [^t002536]
  > But then the success every year you can show for it is, quote, unquote, “nothing happens.” And this is not a very long-lasting policy position, speaking as a politician. [^t002536]
  $a-sept11 [A: the pre-9/11 security analogy] 0.8? @dividends-needed: reinforced cockpit doors before an attack show nothing for their cost; Taiwan's coordination investments instead pay polarization and economic dividends and mitigate extinction risk "as a side effect", which "is much more sustaining" [^t002536]  # kind: analogy
    > This is like before, say, September eleventh. If people advocate for reinforcing airport security, reinforcing cockpit doors, and many other measures, altogether it may cost millions or even billions. [^t002536]
    > So it pays real political dividends along the way and kind of mitigates extinction risk as a side effect, and I think that’s much more sustaining. [^t002536]

# ---- 3. Hyperstition and the optimal level of fear ----

@doom-hyperstition [High collective P(doom) belief is self-fulfilling]: doomerism as hyperstition [^t002739]
  > A hyperstition is a self-fulfilling prophecy. [^t002739]
  $a-hyp [A: the belief-collapse mechanism] 0.85? @doom-hyperstition: "if everybody feels they're doomed and they stop putting energy into actually improving the situation, then we're actually doomed"; converging early on a cosmetic mean makes a bad Schelling point [^t002739] [^t002824]  # kind: mechanism
    > So if everybody feels they’re doomed and they stop putting energy into actually improving the situation, then we’re actually doomed. So a collective belief in a high P(Doom) actually brings about that high P(Doom). [^t002739]
    > But you do not want people to, even before we can reliably measure, even when the variance is very, very high, to kind of believe in a mean point, because when people converge around that mean point, like a Schelling point, it’s usually not a good point. [^t002824]
  @fear-mobilizes [Doom-focus mobilizes prevention]: attention to doom makes people "fight to stop it and then lower the probability" [^t002807]
    > couldn’t you also argue that if a bunch of people focus on AI doom, that’ll just make people fight to stop it and then lower the probability, right? [^t002807]
  $l-feedback [L: the feedback sign is negative] 0.8? ~@doom-hyperstition | @fear-mobilizes: "it's hard to say if it's positive feedback or negative feedback. I would claim it's totally negative feedback" [^t002807]  # kind: testimony
    > It’s hard to say if it’s positive feedback or negative feedback. I would claim it’s totally negative feedback. [^t002807]

@below-optimal-fear [Public concern is below the optimal level]:  # liron: far below, everywhere [^t002959]; audrey: below outside the Taiwanese frontline [^t002922]
  # Overlap discipline: her claim is a SUBSET of his, so the agreed span is
  # one joint factor (author-the-weaker) and his universal strengthening is
  # a single-voice residual re-elicited conditional on the shared part —
  # not two independent full-strength factors.
  $al-below [AL: the agreed span: below optimal off the frontline] 0.75? @below-optimal-fear: both assert it, her explicitly ("where people simply say... 'stochastic parrot'... probably below the optimal level"), his global claim a fortiori; strength from her hedged register (author-the-weaker) [^t002922] [^t002959]  # kind: testimony
    > But in other places, where people simply say, “Oh, it’s just a machine, it cannot do superhuman persuasion, and stochastic parrot, and so on,” then I would say it’s probably below the optimal level. [^t002922]
  $l-everywhere [L: residual: even the aware are far under] 0.7? @below-optimal-fear: his increment beyond the agreed span, "everybody is still way too low... so far under the optimal level of panic", frontline included; residual strength re-elicited conditional on $al-below's span already granted [^t002959]  # kind: testimony
    > And so I actually see—I see us so far under the optimal level of panic, to be honest. [^t002959]

# ---- 4. The capability common ground (the "can" axis) ----
# Shared ground for sections 5 and 7 — every head here stays top-level.

@ceiling-high [The intelligence ceiling is far above humanity]: minds and mind-ensembles vastly outclassing 2025 humanity-in-aggregate are possible [^t004705]
  > Don’t you think that within a few years or decades, a city block of computation will surpass the capabilities of all humans in aggregate who are alive in 2025? [^t004705]
  $al-ceiling [AL: explicit agreement on the ceiling] 0.9? @ceiling-high: a block-sized mound of computation will surpass all humans pooled. "Of course, I agree"; "the scenius is much more intelligent than the genius" [^t004806] [^t004854]  # kind: testimony
    > Of course, I agree. [^t004806]
    > The scenius is much more intelligent than the genius, of course. [^t004854]

@rsi-plausible [A recursive self-improvement run is plausible]: the Claude-90-in-a-week shape of capability jump [^t005008] [^t005125]
  > It doesn’t output anything for a week, and then you come back, and it’s like, “Hey, I just went ahead and coded up Claude 9, which coded up Claude 10, and they started coding each other up faster and faster, and now we’re on Claude 90. I know it took us a year to go from Claude 7 to Claude 8, but now we’re at Claude 90.” [^t005125]
$al-foom [AL: both accept foom] 0.8? @rsi-plausible | @ceiling-high: "there will be a foom"; "you just described civilization... it is quite plausible"; she self-describes "I'm definitely a foomer, even though not a doomer" [^t010323] [^t005208] [^t014904]  # kind: analogy
  > Well, you just described civilization, right? So even before the emergence of machine learning systems, if you plot the scenius of humanity, it also looks like this, right? [^t005208]
  > So yes, it is quite plausible that if you make it, I don’t know, super exponential when it comes to climbing the scale, it is possible. [^t005208]
  > Yeah, I’m definitely a foomer, even though not a doomer. I’m a foomer bloomer. [^t014904]

@deadly-capable [An ideal-algorithm AI could end the world]: world-eating nanotech, or in her fewer words "super hot data center factories, robots that bake the Earth" ("much fewer words, the same effect") [^t010521]
  > Well, I think that’s too many words. Usually, I just say super hot data center factories, robots that bake the Earth. Much fewer words, the same effect. [^t010521]
$al-can [AL: agreement on 'can'] 0.8? @deadly-capable | @ceiling-high: asked whether the ideal program could, if instructed, make world-eating capability: "Yes, but why would we instruct that for starters?" [^t010859] [^t010521]  # kind: testimony
  > Yes, but why would we instruct that for starters? [^t010859]

@can-vs-will [The live dispute is 'will', not 'can']: both are "really bullish on what AI can do with the right steering" and diverge only on what it will be pointed at [^t011119]
  > We’re both really bullish on what AI can do with the right steering, and then where we start to diverge is just on the question of what will it do. We agree on can, and then we have different predictions about will. [^t011119]
  $al-canwill [AL: the factorization is joint] 0.9? @can-vs-will: "We agree on can, and then we have different predictions about will". Her side of it: "Where are you pointing it?" [^t011119] [^t010444]  # kind: testimony
    > Where are you pointing it? Why are you pointing it to the most offense dominant spectrum? [^t010444]

@whether-vs-when [ASI arrival is an easy call; timing is hard]: (id shared with iabied-comprehensive) Tang cites the book approvingly: "it's not a matter of when, but whether" [^t011249]
  > Well, it’s literally not a number, and I think Eliezer agrees with that in his book, “If Anyone Builds It.” He says, “You know, it’s not a matter of when, but whether it would.” [^t011249]
  $al-whether [AL: both endorse the book's framing] 0.85? @whether-vs-when: Shapira adds Yudkowsky's own gloss: the timeline is not load-bearing; "even a few percent in fifty-eight years" warrants the same conversation [^t011307]  # kind: testimony
    > So even if it’s like, yep, there’s still a few percent probability that it happens in fifty-eight years, and we should still be having a pretty similar conversation, even if it’s gonna happen in fifty-eight years. [^t011307]

@foom-soon [The intelligence explosion plausibly lands within a decade]:  # liron: Metaculus consensus ~2032, salient [^t011359]; audrey: "it's literally not a number" [^t011249]
  $l-metaculus [L: the forecaster consensus makes the deadline salient] 0.7? @foom-soon: the Metaculus consensus at 2032 makes the deadline concrete; even if not certain, "your deadline is in seven years" [^t011359] [^t011453]  # kind: empirical
    > Even though it’s not a hundred percent, it’s still salient to be like, look at Metaculus—the consensus is 2032 or something—and you may be an outlier. [^t011359]
    > but your deadline is in seven years, according to Metaculus [^t011359]

# ---- 5. The crux: is steering ready before the jump? ----

@post-attention [Viable post-attention interpretable architectures exist]: e.g. power retention networks (linear memory, arbitrary context, retrainable from a transformer); "it doesn't have to be power retention. It could be anything else" (shared ground: premised by $a-switch here and $a-converge in section 7, so it stays a top-level head)  [^t014538]  # check: 0.5, the Manifold market Tang quotes as her own reading. Its two-year horizon is tighter than this statement, which asks only that a viable architecture exist: she says the candidates exist today and only their commercial availability is open
  > You need to first come up with, for example, a post-transformer, post-attention. For example, just to use a random example, power retention networks by Manifest AI. That’s one of the better candidates. [^t014538]
  > And so it basically says, in two years, there’s, I think, around fifty-fifty chance that we are able then to build state-of-the-art models without depending on the unobservable, almost uninterpretable transformer attention model. [^t014721]

@aligned-in-time [Steering is ready before the decisive jump]: the wrap-up names this the meat of the disagreement: "is that plausible... that we'll get our act together and have it aligned in time?" [^t014826]. Tang declines to price the fork: "the variance is so high for me. I literally don't know" [^t012346] [^t015009]
  > So that was—I think that was the meat of the discussion, is, you know, is that plausible? Is that the mainline scenario, that we’ll get our act together and have it aligned in time? [^t014826]
  > Well, which is why the variance is so high for me. I literally don’t know. [^t012346]
  ::tang-routes [A: how steering gets ready in time]: her battery of routes into the crux, all in one voice: switch to a scrutable architecture, upgrade the governance itself, ride a horizontal takeoff, and peg the takeoff to the governance.
    > So instead of stopping, it’s like collectively steering away from uncertain, but probably doom. [^t014538]
    @arch-switch [Humanity plausibly switches to interpretable architecture in time]: the common-knowledge existence of scrutable alternatives lets policy steer rather than stop [^t014538]
      > So the point is that the existence, even though not at this point the commercial availability of such post-attention scrutable models, I think is an important thing to be put to policymakers as common knowledge. [^t014538]
      @interp-precedent [Earlier architectures were inspectable and steerable]: RNNs and LSTMs: "we have flown other planes, much smaller, before... when we steer toward this place, it's not going to do a sharp left turn" [^t005008]
